questions.cardText:
[Zoology] Why would a hornet attack honey bees?
A. To eat them
B. To feed on their honey
C. To claim the flowers in a territory
Answer: A. Hornets are predators, and often target bee larvae to provide a protein-rich food source for their own larvae. This predation can significantly impact honey bee populations.
questions.en: What do hornets take when they raid honey bee colonies, as protein-rich food for their own larvae?
questions.de: Was holen sich Hornissen, wenn sie Honigbienenvölker überfallen, als eiweißreiche Nahrung für ihre eigenen Larven?
questions.answerEn: The bees themselves (larvae, pupae and adults)
questions.answerDe: Die Bienen selbst (Larven, Puppen und erwachsene Tiere)

timeline.labelEn: Frederick Smith describes the Asian giant hornet (Vespa mandarinia)
timeline.labelDe: Frederick Smith beschreibt die Asiatische Riesenhornisse (Vespa mandarinia)

questions.notes: The Asian giant hornet raids honey bee hives for adults, pupae and larvae to feed its own larvae (the card's explanation mentions only larvae); it also takes honey, but the bees are the protein food.

questions.cardText:
[Religious Studies] What is stigmata in Christianity?
A. A form of divine punishment
B. Miraculous healing
C. The appearance of certain wounds
Answer: C. Saint Francis of Assisi (the namesake of the city of San Francisco) was the first recorded person to receive the stigmata, bearing wounds that resembled those of Christ.
questions.en: In Christianity, what are the bodily wounds called that appear where Christ bore his crucifixion wounds, first recorded in Saint Francis of Assisi?
questions.de: Wie heißen im Christentum die Wunden am Körper, die dort auftreten, wo Christus seine Kreuzigungswunden trug, und die zuerst bei Franz von Assisi bezeugt sind?

timeline.labelEn: Francis of Assisi receives the stigmata after a vision on Mount La Verna (by tradition)
timeline.labelDe: Franz von Assisi empfängt nach einer Vision auf dem Berg La Verna die Stigmata (nach der Überlieferung)

questions.notes: Card's definition question reversed into asking for the term; Francis is widely considered the first recorded stigmatic (17 September 1224 per tradition).
